package_info.package_versions: unknown (affects sites where plugin is installed)
package_info.why_malicious: The plugin is designed solely to defraud website owners by generating and displaying fake ransomware notices on WordPress websites, attempting to extort payment by threatening data loss. It provides no legitimate functionality and is intentionally crafted for fraudulent extortion.

execution_context.trigger: When the plugin is activated or when any page on the site is loaded
required_permissions: Ability to write files to the WordPress plugins directory
Web server access to serve plugin-generated content

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Your Website Has Been Encrypted

To recover your files, send 0.1 bitcoin to the following address...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the plugin is activated or a site page is loaded, the code generates and displays a fake ransomware HTML notice to the website owner, presenting a ransom demand without performing any actual file encryption or modification, resulting in attempted extortion through social engineering.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code displays a ransom demand message to the site owner, which is not a legitimate plugin function and is a clear indicator of a scam. There is no evidence of any real encryption or security feature—only an attempt to coerce payment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate WordPress plugin should provide useful features or enhancements to the website. Displaying extortion messages or ransom demands to administrators or site owners is never acceptable and directly violates user trust and platform guidelines.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins may display admin notices or maintenance messages, but these are informational and never demand payment or threaten data loss. No legitimate plugin displays ransom demands.
key_indicators: Displays a hardcoded ransom demand message to the site owner
No actual file encryption or modification occurs
HTML page is generated and served by the plugin, not by core WordPress functionality
Presence of bitcoin payment instructions in plugin code
Plugin provides no legitimate or expected WordPress functionality

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads and activates the bogus WordPress plugin on the target website.
attack_chain.leads_to: The plugin is installed and ready to execute its malicious payload.

attack_chain.action: Upon activation or when a site page is loaded, the plugin generates and displays an HTML page with a ransom demand, attempting to trick the owner into paying.
attack_chain.leads_to: The website owner is presented with a fake ransomware notice and may be coerced into paying the ransom.

behavioral_signatures: WordPress plugin that displays ransom or extortion notices to administrators or site owners without performing any legitimate function
Plugins generating HTML pages containing bitcoin payment instructions or threats of data loss
file_indicators: Presence of unfamiliar or recently added plugin directories in wp-content/plugins/
Plugin PHP files containing hardcoded ransom messages, bitcoin addresses, or phrases such as 'Your Website Has Been Encrypted'
HTML or PHP files in plugin directories that generate or serve ransom demand content
network_indicators: No outbound network activity required for this scam unless the plugin attempts to contact an external server, which is not mentioned in the report
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or unauthorized plugins in the WordPress installation, especially those that generate or display ransom or extortion messages. Scan plugin files for hardcoded bitcoin addresses, ransom-related keywords, or phrases such as 'Your Website Has Been Encrypted'. Alert on any plugin that displays a ransom demand to administrators or site owners. Regularly audit plugin directories for unfamiliar files or suspicious content.
